title: SQL Aggregates: COUNT, GROUP BY, HAVING and CASE
summary: Quick revision notes on SQL aggregate functions, grouping, HAVING vs WHERE, DISTINCT, CASE expressions and how NULLs affect counts. Ends with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Aggregates and the Grouping Mental Model
points: An aggregate function collapses many rows into one value: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX
Without GROUP BY, the whole table is one group and returns exactly one row
GROUP BY splits rows into buckets by column values; each bucket yields one output row

Portable rule: every non-aggregated column in SELECT should appear in GROUP BY (PostgreSQL and MySQL 5.7+ also accept columns functionally dependent on the grouped key, SQLite accepts bare columns, SQL Server is strict)
Logical order: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY

chapters.title: Core Aggregate Functions
points: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(col) counts non-NULL values in col
SUM(col) and AVG(col) ignore NULLs; AVG = SUM / COUNT(col), not row count
MIN and MAX work on numbers, strings and dates, and ignore NULLs
SUM, AVG and MAX over zero rows return NULL, but COUNT returns 0
Example: SELECT dept, COUNT(*), AVG(salary), MAX(salary) FROM emp GROUP BY dept;

chapters.title: WHERE vs HAVING
points: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation
Aggregates are allowed in HAVING but not in WHERE
Example: SELECT dept, COUNT(*) FROM emp WHERE active = 1 GROUP BY dept HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;
Put non-aggregate conditions in WHERE: it shrinks the data before grouping and is faster
HAVING without GROUP BY treats the whole table as a single group

chapters.title: DISTINCT and Counting with NULLs
points: SELECT DISTINCT col removes duplicate rows; it applies to the whole select list, not just the first column
COUNT(DISTINCT col) counts unique non-NULL values
COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col) vs COUNT(DISTINCT col) give three different numbers when NULLs and duplicates exist
NULL = NULL is not true; use IS NULL, though GROUP BY and DISTINCT treat all NULLs as one group
Count NULLs with SUM(CASE WHEN col IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) or COUNT(*) - COUNT(col)

chapters.title: CASE Expressions and Conditional Aggregation
points: CASE WHEN cond THEN x WHEN cond2 THEN y ELSE z END returns the first matching branch
Without ELSE, unmatched rows return NULL
Conditional count: SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'paid' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
Pivot-style: SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2024 THEN amt END) AS y2024 per column
CASE can appear in SELECT, ORDER BY, GROUP BY and inside aggregates

chapters.title: Aggregates Cheat Sheet
points: COUNT(*) all rows; COUNT(col) non-NULL; COUNT(DISTINCT col) unique non-NULL
SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX skip NULLs; empty input gives NULL except COUNT gives 0
WHERE filters rows before GROUP BY; HAVING filters groups after
Select list columns are either in GROUP BY or inside an aggregate
Conditional aggregate: SUM(CASE WHEN cond THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
Interview Point: Why does AVG differ from SUM/COUNT(*) with NULLs, and when do you use HAVING instead of WHERE?
